subproblem.title: Vanishing n-density of μ in the cone around the normal space at a tangent point (Remark 1.5(3), cone part)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Let x ∈ ℝ^N, P a linear subspace of ℝ^N and θ ∈ ℝ such that HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ holds (finrank P = n and (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ(y) → θ ∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x), Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let q_P = P.starProjection be the orthogonal projection onto P and C_x := {z : |q_P(z − x)| ≤ |z − x|/2}. Then for every ε > 0, μ(C_x ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ε ρⁿ (as ENNReal.ofReal(ερⁿ)) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0, i.e. eventually in 𝓝[>] 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (x : Rn N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)) (θ : ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → 0 < n → HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μ ({z | ‖P.starProjection (z - x)‖ ≤ ‖z - x‖ / 2} ∩ Metric.ball x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ε * ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 3 (6′) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 97–105: approximate the indicator of X_{1/2}((T_xM)^⊥, 0) ∩ B_1(0) by test functions), with multiplicity θ. The parent's dominated-convergence step is replaced by the explicit estimate of Steps 1 and 4–5 below.

Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm, q := q_P, and ν := Hⁿ⌞P = μHE[n].restrict P, so ∫_P f dHⁿ = ∫ f dν. Recall that |q v| ≤ |v| for all v (Mathlib `Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le`) and q w = w for w ∈ P (`Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff`).

1. ν is small near 0. Because finrank P = n, ν is finite on compact sets (SimonGMT `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule`). Because n ≥ 1, the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure has no atoms (Mathlib `Measure.nullSingletonClass_hausdorff`), and μHE[n] is a scalar multiple of it, so ν({0}) ≤ μHE[n]({0}) = 0. The closed balls B̄_{1/(k+1)}(0), k ∈ ℕ, decrease, their intersection is {0}, and ν(B̄_1(0)) < ∞; by continuity from above (Mathlib `tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop`) ν(B̄_{1/(k+1)}(0)) → 0. Hence there is k ∈ ℕ with |θ| · ν(B̄_{1/(k+1)}(0)) < ε/2 (ν-values being finite reals). Put r := 1/(3(k+1)) > 0, so that 3r = 1/(k+1).

2. Cone and test function. Let S := {w : |q w| ≤ |w|/2} ∩ B̄_1(0). Then 0 ∈ S, so S ≠ ∅. Define f(w) := max(0, 1 − dist(w, S)/r). Since w ↦ dist(w, S) is 1-Lipschitz, f is continuous; 0 ≤ f ≤ 1; f = 1 on S (there dist(w, S) = 0); and f(w) = 0 whenever dist(w, S) ≥ r.

3. Compact support. If |w| > 1 + r, then dist(w, S) ≥ r: otherwise some s ∈ S has |w − s| < r, and then |w| ≤ |w − s| + |s| < r + 1, a contradiction. So f vanishes outside the compact ball B̄_{1+r}(0), and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).

4. Localization on P. If w ∈ P and f(w) ≠ 0, then |w| < 3r. Indeed dist(w, S) < r gives s ∈ S with |w − s| < r. Then |w| = |q w| ≤ |q s| + |q(w − s)| ≤ |s|/2 + |w − s|, and |s| ≤ |w| + |w − s|; hence |w| ≤ |w|/2 + (3/2)|w − s| < |w|/2 + 3r/2, i.e. |w| < 3r.

5. Bound for the limit. By step 4 and 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, for every w ∈ P (so for ν-a.e. w) we have f(w) ≤ 1_{B̄_{3r}(0)}(w). Since ν(B̄_{3r}(0)) < ∞, monotonicity of the integral gives 0 ≤ ∫_P f dHⁿ ≤ ν(B̄_{3r}(0)). Therefore L := θ ∫_P f dHⁿ ≤ |θ| ∫_P f dHⁿ ≤ |θ| ν(B̄_{1/(k+1)}(0)) < ε/2 < ε.

6. Blow-up limit. By the hypothesis applied to f, (ρⁿ)⁻¹ J(ρ) → L as ρ ↓ 0, where J(ρ) := ∫ f(η_{x,ρ}(y)) dμ(y). Since L < ε there is ρ₀ > 0 with (ρⁿ)⁻¹ J(ρ) < ε, i.e. J(ρ) < ε ρⁿ, for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀).

7. Comparison. Fix ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀) and let T := C_x ∩ B_ρ(x). T is Borel (C_x is closed) and μ(T) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) < ∞. If y ∈ T and w := η_{x,ρ}(y) = ρ⁻¹(y − x), then |w| = |y − x|/ρ < 1 and |q w| = ρ⁻¹|q(y − x)| ≤ ρ⁻¹|y − x|/2 = |w|/2, so w ∈ S and f(w) = 1. Hence 1_T ≤ f∘η_{x,ρ} pointwise (f ≥ 0). The function f∘η_{x,ρ} is continuous and, by step 3, vanishes outside the compact ball B̄_{ρ(1+r)}(x); as μ is finite on compact sets it is μ-integrable. Therefore μ(T) = ∫ 1_T dμ ≤ J(ρ) < ε ρⁿ, i.e. μ(C_x ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(ε ρⁿ) for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀). ∎

subproblem.title: Key cone estimate: uniform density and cone bounds force a projection lower bound (Simon (9)–(10), corrected constant)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^N with orthogonal projection q = Q.starProjection, let E ⊆ ℝ^N, and let a, b, δ ∈ ℝ with a > 0 and 32ⁿ b < a. Assume that for every x ∈ E and every ρ ∈ (0, δ): (9a) μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ a ρⁿ, and (9b) μ({z : |q(z − x)| ≤ |z − x|/3} ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ b ρⁿ (both read in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(…) and μ(…) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(bρⁿ)). Then |y − x| ≤ 4 |q(y − x)| for all x, y ∈ E with |y − x| < δ/2.

Source. This is Step 5 (Claim (10′)) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon's (9)–(10) (chapter-03.txt lines 212–249) with the parent's departure (a) (Simon's ε = 1/16ⁿ is too large; the parent takes a = (1 − ε)2^k ω_n, b = ε 2^k ω_n with ε = 1/(2(1 + 32ⁿ)), for which 32ⁿ b < a) and departure (b) (cones around a fixed plane Q with aperture 1/3 and the ball B_{ρ/16}(y)). Here a and b are arbitrary with a > 0 and 32ⁿ b < a.

1. Let x, y ∈ E with |y − x| < δ/2, and suppose for a contradiction that |y − x| > 4 |q(y − x)|. Put ρ := |y − x|. Then ρ > 4|q(y − x)| ≥ 0, so ρ > 0 and |q(y − x)| < ρ/4; also ρ < δ/2.

2. Inclusion. Let C := {z : |q(z − x)| ≤ |z − x|/3}. We claim B_{ρ/16}(y) ⊆ C ∩ B_{2ρ}(x). Let |z − y| < ρ/16. (i) |z − x| ≤ |z − y| + |y − x| < ρ/16 + ρ < 2ρ. (ii) |z − x| ≥ |y − x| − |z − y| > ρ − ρ/16 = 15ρ/16. (iii) q is linear and |q v| ≤ |v| for all v (orthogonal projection; Mathlib `Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le`), so |q(z − x)| ≤ |q(y − x)| + |q(z − y)| ≤ |q(y − x)| + |z − y| < ρ/4 + ρ/16 = 5ρ/16 = (15ρ/16)/3 < |z − x|/3. Hence z ∈ C ∩ B_{2ρ}(x).

3. Both radii ρ/16 and 2ρ lie in (0, δ), since 0 < ρ < δ/2. Applying (9a) at y with radius ρ/16, monotonicity of μ together with step 2, and (9b) at x with radius 2ρ, we get
   ENNReal.ofReal(a (ρ/16)ⁿ) ≤ μ(B_{ρ/16}(y)) ≤ μ(C ∩ B_{2ρ}(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(b (2ρ)ⁿ).

4. Since a (ρ/16)ⁿ > 0, the inequality ENNReal.ofReal(a(ρ/16)ⁿ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(b(2ρ)ⁿ) implies a (ρ/16)ⁿ ≤ b (2ρ)ⁿ (Mathlib `ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff'`). As (2ρ)ⁿ = 32ⁿ (ρ/16)ⁿ and (ρ/16)ⁿ > 0, this gives a ≤ 32ⁿ b, contradicting the hypothesis 32ⁿ b < a.

5. Therefore |y − x| ≤ 4 |q(y − x)| for all x, y ∈ E with |y − x| < δ/2 (for y = x this reads 0 ≤ 0). ∎

subproblem.title: A set on which the projection to an n-plane is locally co-Lipschitz lies in countably many Lipschitz images of ℝⁿ
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with finrank Q = n and orthogonal projection q = Q.starProjection, let E ⊆ ℝ^N, C ∈ ℝ and δ > 0, and assume |y − x| ≤ C |q(y − x)| for all x, y ∈ E with |y − x| < δ. Then there are maps F_0, F_1, F_2, … : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), each Lipschitz (with some constant K_i ≥ 0), such that E ⊆ ⋃_i F_i(ℝⁿ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)) (E : Set (Rn N)) (C δ : ℝ), finrank ℝ Q = n → 0 < δ → (∀ x ∈ E, ∀ y ∈ E, ‖y - x‖ < δ → ‖y - x‖ ≤ C * ‖Q.starProjection (y - x)‖) → ∃ F : ℕ → Rn n → Rn N, (∀ i, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzWith K (F i)) ∧ E ⊆ ⋃ i, Set.range (F i)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 6 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon chapter-03.txt lines 249–262 ((10) together with the extension theorem 1.2 of Ch. 2 shows that E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) lies in a Lipschitz graph over the plane, and finitely many such graphs cover E). The parent covers a compact E by finitely many balls; here an arbitrary E is covered by countably many balls using separability of ℝ^N, which is all the parent needs. The parent applies this with C = 4 and δ replaced by δ/2.

1. Coordinates. Put C′ := max(C, 0) ≥ 0; the hypothesis also holds with C′ in place of C. Since finrank Q = n, there is a linear isometric isomorphism ι : ℝⁿ → Q (for instance the inverse of the coordinate map of an orthonormal basis of Q indexed by Fin n, `((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q).reindex (finCongr _)).repr.symm`). Let π : ℝ^N → Q be the orthogonal projection onto Q regarded as an element of Q (`Q.orthogonalProjectionOnto`, so that π(y) = q(y) as vectors of ℝ^N), and p := ι⁻¹ ∘ π : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ. Since ι⁻¹ is a linear isometry, |p(y) − p(y′)| = |q(y − y′)| for all y, y′ ∈ ℝ^N.

2. Pieces. Let D ⊆ ℝ^N be a countable dense set (ℝ^N is separable; Mathlib `TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense`); D ≠ ∅. For d ∈ D put S_d := E ∩ B_{δ/2}(d). For y, y′ ∈ S_d we have |y − y′| ≤ |y − d| + |d − y′| < δ, hence by the hypothesis and step 1, |y − y′| ≤ C′ |p(y) − p(y′)|.

3. Lipschitz inverse. Choose h_d : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N with h_d(w) ∈ S_d and p(h_d(w)) = w for every w ∈ p(S_d) (choice; Mathlib `Function.invFunOn p S_d`). For w, w′ ∈ p(S_d), step 2 applied to h_d(w), h_d(w′) ∈ S_d gives |h_d(w) − h_d(w′)| ≤ C′ |p(h_d(w)) − p(h_d(w′))| = C′ |w − w′|. Thus h_d is C′-Lipschitz on p(S_d).

4. Extension. Since the target ℝ^N is finite-dimensional, h_d restricted to p(S_d) extends to a Lipschitz map F_d : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N with F_d = h_d on p(S_d) (Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension`; equivalently Simon Ch. 2 Thm 1.2 / McShane's extension applied to each coordinate). If y ∈ S_d, then y′ := F_d(p(y)) = h_d(p(y)) ∈ S_d and p(y′) = p(y), so |y′ − y| ≤ C′ |p(y′) − p(y)| = 0 by step 2, i.e. y = F_d(p(y)) ∈ F_d(ℝⁿ). Hence S_d ⊆ F_d(ℝⁿ).

5. Covering. For x ∈ E, density of D gives d ∈ D with |x − d| < δ/2, i.e. x ∈ S_d. Hence E ⊆ ⋃_{d ∈ D} F_d(ℝⁿ). Enumerate the countable nonempty set D as D = {d_i : i ∈ ℕ} (Mathlib `Set.Countable.exists_eq_range`) and put F_i := F_{d_i}. Each F_i is Lipschitz and E ⊆ ⋃_i F_i(ℝⁿ). ∎

Remark. F_d(ℝⁿ) contains Simon's Lipschitz graph piece over Q (up to the reparametrization ι). Closedness of the graphs is not needed: the parent obtains Borel measurability of the final union from σ-compactness of continuous images of ℝⁿ.

subproblem.title: Positive lower n-density at a point with an approximate tangent plane of positive multiplicity (Remark 1.5(3), lower half)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Let x ∈ ℝ^N, P a linear subspace of ℝ^N and θ > 0 such that HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ holds, i.e. finrank P = n and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ(y) → θ ∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then there is c > 0 such that μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ c ρⁿ (precisely ENNReal.ofReal(c ρⁿ) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)), B_ρ(x) the open ball) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0, i.e. eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (x : Rn N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)) (θ : ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → 0 < θ → HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal (c * ρ ^ n) ≤ μ (Metric.ball x ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the lower half of Step 3 (5′) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 91–97: test functions f ∈ C_c with values in [0, 1] comparing ∫ f∘η_{x,ρ} with the mass of a ball), written with multiplicity θ and for every n ≥ 0. Only the lower bound for μ(B_ρ(x)) is needed by the parent, so no two-sided density limit is proved.

Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm, B_ρ(x) the open and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball, and ν := Hⁿ⌞P = μHE[n].restrict P, so that ∫_P f dHⁿ = ∫ f dν.

1. Test function. Define g(w) := max(0, 1 − |w|) for w ∈ ℝ^N. Then g is continuous, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g(w) = 0 whenever |w| ≥ 1, and g(w) > 0 whenever |w| < 1. Since g vanishes outside the compact set B̄_1(0), g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).

2. The plane measure. Because finrank P = n, the measure ν is regular, in particular finite on compact sets, and its support is exactly P (SimonGMT `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule` and `support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule`; mathematically: the isometric inclusion P ↪ ℝ^N carries μHE[n] of the n-dimensional inner product space P, which is its Lebesgue (Haar) measure, onto ν). Consequently g, being continuous with compact support, is ν-integrable.

3. ∫_P g dHⁿ > 0. Since 0 ∈ P = spt ν and B_1(0) is a neighbourhood of 0, ν(B_1(0)) > 0. Moreover g ≥ 0 and {w : g(w) ≠ 0} ⊇ B_1(0). A nonnegative integrable function has positive integral as soon as its support has positive measure (Mathlib `integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg`), so ∫_P g dHⁿ = ∫ g dν > 0.

4. Choice of c. Put L := θ ∫_P g dHⁿ; then L > 0 because θ > 0. Put c := L/2 > 0. By the hypothesis applied to f = g, (ρⁿ)⁻¹ I(ρ) → L as ρ ↓ 0, where I(ρ) := ∫ g(η_{x,ρ}(y)) dμ(y). Since L/2 < L, there is ρ₀ > 0 such that (ρⁿ)⁻¹ I(ρ) > L/2 for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀); multiplying by ρⁿ > 0 gives c ρⁿ < I(ρ) for ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀).

5. Comparison with the ball. Fix ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀). The closed ball B̄_ρ(x) is compact, so μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) < ∞. If y ∉ B_ρ(x), then |η_{x,ρ}(y)| = |y − x|/ρ ≥ 1 and hence g(η_{x,ρ}(y)) = 0; if y ∈ B_ρ(x), then g(η_{x,ρ}(y)) ≤ 1. Hence 0 ≤ g∘η_{x,ρ} ≤ 1_{B_ρ(x)} pointwise. The indicator 1_{B_ρ(x)} is μ-integrable (finite measure), so monotonicity of the integral for a nonnegative minorant (Mathlib `integral_mono_of_nonneg`) gives I(ρ) ≤ ∫ 1_{B_ρ(x)} dμ = μ(B_ρ(x)) (the latter as a finite real number; Mathlib `integral_indicator_one`).

6. Conclusion. For every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀) we have c ρⁿ < I(ρ) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞, hence ENNReal.ofReal(c ρⁿ) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)). Thus c > 0 and the inequality holds eventually in 𝓝[>] 0. (For n = 0 nothing changes: ρ⁰ = 1, P = {0} and ν = H⁰⌞{0} is the unit point mass at 0.) ∎

subproblem.title: A countable ε-net of n-planes for the orthogonal-projection norm
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ with n ≤ N and let ε > 0. Then there is a sequence Q_0, Q_1, Q_2, … of linear subspaces of ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), each of dimension n, such that every n-dimensional linear subspace P of ℝ^N satisfies ‖q_P − q_{Q_j}‖ < ε for some j ∈ ℕ, where q_V = V.starProjection : ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^N is the orthogonal projection onto V and ‖·‖ is the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ), n ≤ N → 0 < ε → ∃ Q : ℕ → Submodule ℝ (Rn N), (∀ j, finrank ℝ (Q j) = n) ∧ ∀ P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N), finrank ℝ P = n → ∃ j, ‖P.starProjection - (Q j).starProjection‖ < ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the first paragraph of Step 4 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon p. 73 (chapter-03.txt lines 222–228: choose planes π_1, …, π_N such that every plane is within 1/16 of one of them, in the distance d(π, π′) = ‖q_π − q_{π′}‖ of (3)). The parent obtains finitely many planes by compactness; countably many suffice for the parent, and they are obtained here from separability. The parent uses ε = 1/16.

1. Let 𝒜 := {q_P : P a linear subspace of ℝ^N with finrank P = n}, a subset of the normed space L := (ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^N). Since L is finite-dimensional it is a separable metric space, so every subset of L is separable; and a separable subset of a pseudo-metrizable space contains a countable subset dense in it. Hence there is a countable set 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒜 with 𝒜 ⊆ closure(𝒟) (Mathlib `TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.of_separableSpace` and `TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset`).

2. 𝒜 is nonempty. Since n ≤ N = finrank ℝ^N, there are linearly independent vectors v_1, …, v_n in ℝ^N (Mathlib `exists_linearIndependent_of_le_finrank`), and P₀ := span{v_1, …, v_n} has finrank n (Mathlib `finrank_span_eq_card`). Thus q_{P₀} ∈ 𝒜.

3. 𝒟 is nonempty: if 𝒟 = ∅ then closure(𝒟) = ∅, which cannot contain q_{P₀} ∈ 𝒜. A countable nonempty set is the range of a sequence, so 𝒟 = {d_j : j ∈ ℕ} for some sequence (d_j) (Mathlib `Set.Countable.exists_eq_range`).

4. For each j, d_j ∈ 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒜, so we may choose a linear subspace Q_j with finrank Q_j = n and q_{Q_j} = d_j.

5. Let P be an n-dimensional subspace. Then q_P ∈ 𝒜 ⊆ closure(𝒟), so by the metric characterization of the closure there is d ∈ 𝒟 with dist(q_P, d) < ε. Writing d = d_j = q_{Q_j}, we get ‖q_P − q_{Q_j}‖ = dist(q_P, q_{Q_j}) < ε. ∎

```lean
theorem Submission.tangentMeasure_countable_projection_net : (∀ (N n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ), n ≤ N → 0 < ε → ∃ Q : ℕ → Submodule ℝ (Rn N), (∀ j, finrank ℝ (Q j) = n) ∧ ∀ P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N), finrank ℝ P = n → ∃ j, ‖P.starProjection - (Q j).starProjection‖ < ε) := by
  intro N n ε hnN hε
  classical
  let S : Set (Rn N →L[ℝ] Rn N) :=
    (fun P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N) => P.starProjection) '' {P | finrank ℝ P = n}
  obtain ⟨D, hDS, hDc, hSD⟩ :=
    (TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.of_separableSpace S).exists_countable_dense_subset
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_linearIndependent_of_le_finrank (R := ℝ) (M := Rn N) (n := n)
    (by simpa [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin] using hnN)
  have hP0 : finrank ℝ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range f)) = n := by
    rw [finrank_span_eq_card hf, Fintype.card_fin]
  have hSne : S.Nonempty := ⟨_, ⟨_, hP0, rfl⟩⟩
  have hDne : D.Nonempty := by
    by_contra h
    rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at h
    obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := hSne
    have := hSD hT
    rw [h, closure_empty] at this
    exact this
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hDc.exists_eq_range hDne
  have hmemS : ∀ j, ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Rn N), finrank ℝ Q = n ∧ Q.starProjection = e j := by
    intro j
    have : e j ∈ S := hDS (he ▸ Set.mem_range_self j)
    obtain ⟨Q, hQ, hQe⟩ := this
    exact ⟨Q, hQ, hQe⟩
  choose Q hQdim hQe using hmemS
  refine ⟨Q, hQdim, fun P hP => ?_⟩
  have hPS : P.starProjection ∈ S := ⟨P, hP, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨T, hTD, hdist⟩ := Metric.mem_closure_iff.mp (hSD hPS) ε hε
  rw [he] at hTD
  obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hTD
  refine ⟨j, ?_⟩
  rw [hQe j, ← dist_eq_norm]
  exact hdist
```
proof_key_steps: The set 𝒜 of orthogonal projections onto n-planes is a subset of the finite-dimensional, hence separable, operator space, so it contains a countable dense subset 𝒟.
n ≤ N gives an n-plane, so 𝒜 and 𝒟 are nonempty; enumerate 𝒟 = {d_j} and choose n-planes Q_j with q_{Q_j} = d_j.
Density of 𝒟 in 𝒜 gives, for each n-plane P, some j with ‖q_P − q_{Q_j}‖ < ε.

subproblem.title: Zero-dimensional case: a locally finite measure with positive lower 0-density a.e. is carried by a countable, countably 0-rectifiable Borel set
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Assume that for μ-a.e. x there is c > 0 such that μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ c (as ENNReal.ofReal c ≤ μ(B_ρ(x))) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0. Then there is a Borel set R ⊆ ℝ^N which is countably 0-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable 0 R) and satisfies μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)), (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal c ≤ μ (Metric.ball x ρ)) → ∃ R : Set (Rn N), MeasurableSet R ∧ CountablyRectifiable 0 R ∧ μ Rᶜ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 2 (case n = 0) of the parent proof. In the parent, the hypothesis of this child is supplied by the lower-density child applied with n = 0 (ρ⁰ = 1); the parent shows μ({x}) > 0 a.e. and takes R to be the set of atoms.

1. Atoms. Let x satisfy the hypothesis with constant c > 0 and threshold ρ₀ > 0, i.e. μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ c for 0 < ρ < ρ₀. For any r > 0, ρ := min(r/2, ρ₀/2) lies in (0, ρ₀) and ρ < r, so μ(B_r(x)) ≥ μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ c. The open balls B_{1/(k+1)}(x), k ∈ ℕ, decrease; their intersection is {x} (if y ≠ x choose k with 1/(k+1) < |y − x|); and μ(B_1(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_1(x)) < ∞ since B̄_1(x) is compact. By continuity from above (Mathlib `Antitone.measure_iInter`), μ({x}) = inf_k μ(B_{1/(k+1)}(x)) ≥ c > 0. Hence μ({x}) > 0 for μ-a.e. x.

2. Countably many atoms. μ is finite on compact sets, hence locally finite, hence σ-finite because ℝ^N is σ-compact (Mathlib instance `sigmaFinite_of_locallyFinite`), in particular s-finite. The singletons {x}, x ∈ ℝ^N, form a family of pairwise disjoint measurable sets, so only countably many of them have positive measure (Mathlib `Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion`; elementarily, B̄_k(0) contains at most m μ(B̄_k(0)) points of mass ≥ 1/m). Thus R := {x : μ({x}) > 0} is countable.

3. R is Borel, being a countable union of closed singletons. By step 1, ℝ^N ∖ R = {x : μ({x}) = 0} is μ-null, i.e. μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0.

4. Countable 0-rectifiability. Take the exceptional set M₀ := ∅ (H⁰(∅) = 0). If R = ∅, the constant maps F_j ≡ 0 : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^N work. Otherwise write R = {e_j : j ∈ ℕ} (Mathlib `Set.Countable.exists_eq_range`) and let F_j : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^N be the constant map with value e_j; it is Lipschitz with constant 0, and since ℝ⁰ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is nonempty (it contains 0), e_j ∈ F_j(ℝ⁰). Hence R ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰), which is Definition 1.1 with n = 0, i.e. CountablyRectifiable 0 R. ∎

```lean
  intro N μ hfin hae
  haveI : IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ := ⟨hfin⟩
  have hatom : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < μ {x} := by
    filter_upwards [hae] with x hx
    obtain ⟨c, hc, hev⟩ := hx
    obtain ⟨ρ₀, hρ₀, hρ₀'⟩ := (nhdsGT_basis (0 : ℝ)).eventually_iff.mp hev
    have hall : ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ENNReal.ofReal c ≤ μ (Metric.ball x r) := by
      intro r hr
      have hmin : min (r / 2) (ρ₀ / 2) ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ρ₀ :=
        ⟨by positivity, lt_of_le_of_lt (min_le_right _ _) (by linarith)⟩
      exact (hρ₀' hmin).trans (measure_mono (Metric.ball_subset_ball
        ((min_le_left _ _).trans (by linarith))))
    have hanti : Antitone (fun k : ℕ => Metric.ball x (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1))) := by
      intro k l hkl
      apply Metric.ball_subset_ball
      gcongr
    have hinter : (⋂ k : ℕ, Metric.ball x (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1))) = {x} := by
      ext y
      simp only [Set.mem_iInter, Metric.mem_ball, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      constructor
      · intro h
        by_contra hne
        have hpos : 0 < dist y x := dist_pos.mpr hne
        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_nat_one_div_lt hpos
        exact absurd (h k) (not_lt.mpr hk.le)
      · rintro rfl k
        simp only [dist_self]
        positivity
    have hlim : μ {x} = ⨅ k : ℕ, μ (Metric.ball x (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1))) := by
      rw [← hinter]
      exact hanti.measure_iInter (fun k => measurableSet_ball.nullMeasurableSet)
        ⟨0, (measure_mono Metric.ball_subset_closedBall).trans_lt
          (isCompact_closedBall x _).measure_lt_top |>.ne⟩
    rw [hlim]
    exact lt_of_lt_of_le (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hc) (le_iInf fun k => hall _ (by positivity))
  set R := {x : Rn N | 0 < μ {x}} with hRdef
  have hRc : R.Countable := by
    have := Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion (μ := μ)
      (As := fun x : Rn N => ({x} : Set (Rn N))) (fun x => measurableSet_singleton x)
      (fun x y hxy => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hxy)
    simpa using this
  refine ⟨R, hRc.measurableSet, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rcases R.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hR | hR
    · rw [hR]
      exact ⟨∅, measure_empty, fun _ _ => 0, fun _ => ⟨0, LipschitzWith.const 0⟩, by simp⟩
    · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hRc.exists_eq_range hR
      refine ⟨∅, measure_empty, fun j _ => e j, fun j => ⟨0, LipschitzWith.const _⟩, ?_⟩
      intro x hx
      rw [he] at hx
      obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hx
      exact Or.inr (Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩)
  · rw [ae_iff] at hatom
    refine measure_mono_null (fun x hx => ?_) hatom
```

proof_key_steps: A uniform lower bound for μ(B_ρ(x)) at small radii and local finiteness give μ({x}) ≥ c > 0 by continuity from above.
μ is σ-finite, so the set R of atoms of μ is countable.
R is Borel and μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0 by the first step.
A countable set is covered by the ranges of constant (Lipschitz) maps ℝ⁰ → ℝ^N, hence is countably 0-rectifiable.
